questions.q: Which type of specification focuses on the final functional outcome and required results rather than the specific methods or materials used to achieve them?
questions.n: This type defines the required behavior or result, giving the contractor the flexibility to choose the means and methods.

questions.q: A specification that lists a specific product by brand name, model number, and manufacturer is known as what?
questions.n: Proprietary specs lock in a specific product, often used when a very particular aesthetic or performance match is needed.

questions.q: Under the MasterFormat system, which Division covers the 'General Requirements' for the entire project?
questions.n: Division 01 is dedicated to General Requirements, including administrative and procedural elements that apply to all sections.

questions.q: Which type of specification provides detailed descriptions of materials, workmanship, installation, and equipment, effectively telling the contractor exactly 'how to do it'?
questions.n: Also known as closed or descriptive specs, these prescribe the exact means and materials to be used.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of 'Outline Specifications' produced during the Schematic Design or Design Development phases?
o: To list the contact information for all subcontractors
To define the general scope and quality of materials for cost estimating
To provide a record of submittals approved by the architect
To serve as the final contract document for bidding
questions.n: Outline specs help establish the quality level early on so the owner and estimators understand the project's direction.

questions.q: Division 01 often includes requirements for 'Submittals.' Which of the following is considered a submittal?
questions.n: Shop drawings are prepared by the contractor or vendor to show how they intend to execute a specific part of the work.

questions.q: Which section of Division 01 would typically cover the procedures for requesting a substitution of a material specified in the contract?
questions.n: This section outlines how products are chosen and the administrative steps for proposing 'equal' alternatives.

questions.q: In the Three-Part Section Format used for technical specifications, what is the title of 'Part 2'?
questions.n: Part 2 is 'Products,' which lists the materials, equipment, and manufactured items required.

questions.q: Which document contains the bidding requirements, contract forms, conditions of the contract, and the specifications?
questions.n: The Project Manual is the bound volume containing all written legal and technical documents for the project.

questions.q: Division 01 'Quality Requirements' typically addresses which of the following activities?
questions.n: This section coordinates how materials are tested (e.g., concrete strength) to ensure they meet the specs.

questions.q: Which document is often referred to as the 'Constitution' of a construction project, defining the legal rights and responsibilities of the owner, architect, and contractor?
questions.n: General Conditions (like AIA A201) establish the legal relationships and rights that govern the entire project lifecycle.

questions.q: In MasterFormat, which section is used to describe a change in the project scope where the owner has a choice between different materials or systems for a price difference?
questions.n: Alternates (Section 01 23 00) allow the owner to select between different options, affecting the total contract sum.

questions.q: Which part of the Project Manual contains the 'Instructions to Bidders' and 'Bid Forms'?
questions.n: Division 00 (Procurement and Contracting Requirements) covers everything needed to bid on the project.

questions.q: When a specification relies on established industry tests like ASTM or ANSI without naming a specific manufacturer, what is it called?
questions.n: This type uses recognized industry standards to ensure quality while allowing for open competition among manufacturers.

questions.q: Under Division 01, which section governs the final walk-through and the creation of a 'punch list'?
questions.n: Section 01 77 00 covers the administrative steps for substantial completion, including the punch list.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) in Division 01?
o: QA is about the process; QC is about the final product.
QA is done by the contractor; QC is done by the architect.
There is no difference; they are interchangeable terms.
QA only applies to materials; QC only applies to labor.
questions.n: QA establishes the standards and procedures (preventative), while QC involves testing the actual work (detection).

questions.q: Which Division 01 section would include requirements for a project billboard or site signage?
questions.n: Section 01 58 00 specifically dictates the size, design, and location of project signs and billboards.

questions.q: In the 'Three-Part Section Format,' which part contains information on 'Submittals' and 'Quality Assurance' for that specific section?
questions.n: Part 1 covers the administrative, procedural, and temporary requirements specific to that section.

questions.q: Which of the following is typically a 'Construction Aid' found under Division 01?
questions.n: Construction aids (Section 01 54 00) are temporary tools like hoists, scaffolding, and cranes used to build the project.

questions.q: If a contractor wants to use a different manufacturer than the three listed in a 'Base Bid' specification, what process must they follow?
questions.n: Section 01 25 00 outlines how a contractor can propose an 'or equal' product for approval by the architect.

questions.q: In the CSI MasterFormat, which specific section within Division 01 typically addresses the 'price and payment procedures,' including the Schedule of Values?
questions.n: This section establishes the administrative requirements for applications for payment and the detailed breakdown of costs.

questions.q: When an architect specifies a 'Cash Allowance' in Division 01, what is they primarily accounting for?
o: A monetary sum for items whose exact selection hasn't been made yet
The cost of architectural design fees
A specific manufacturer that must be used regardless of cost
The contractor's overhead and profit for the entire project
questions.n: Allowances cover the purchase price of materials (like hardware or tile) when the final choice is delayed until later in construction.

questions.q: Which document is maintained by the contractor on-site to record the 'actual' locations of concealed items and any deviations from the original design?
questions.n: Often called 'As-Builts,' these documents record exactly where pipes, conduits, and structures were installed.

questions.q: If a specification section requires 'Certified Test Reports,' in which part of the 3-Part Section Format would this requirement be found?
questions.n: Submittal requirements and quality assurance documentation standards are always located in the General part of a section.

questions.q: Which type of meeting, usually required by Division 01, is held before a specific, complex trade starts their work (e.g., roofing or waterproofing)?
questions.n: These are held to review site conditions, submittals, and installation procedures with the specific subcontractors involved.

questions.q: Which organization is responsible for maintaining the 'MasterFormat' and 'SectionFormat' standards used in the Philippines and the US?
o: ASTM (American Society for Testing and Materials)
questions.n: CSI, along with CSC in Canada, created and maintains the organizational standards for specifications.

questions.q: Under Division 01, who is typically responsible for providing 'Temporary Utilities' (water, power, heat) during construction?
questions.n: Unless stated otherwise, the contractor must arrange and often pay for the temporary power and water needed to perform the work.

questions.q: Which of the following would be categorized as a 'Procedural' requirement in Division 01?
o: The process for submitting a Request for Information (RFI)
The brand of paint to be used
The depth of a foundation footing
questions.n: RFIs are administrative communications, which are a core focus of Division 01.

questions.q: In a specification section, where would you find the requirements for a manufacturer's 'Extended Warranty'?
questions.n: Warranties are administrative items that define the duration and terms of coverage, which belong in Part 1.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of 'Division 01' in the Project Manual?
o: To provide the structural calculations for the building
To serve as the architectural design philosophy statement
To list every single screw and nail needed for the project
To bridge the gap between the legal contract and the technical specifications
questions.n: Division 01 explains how to implement the legal rules (General Conditions) during the technical work (Divisions 02-49).

questions.q: Which section in Division 01 covers the requirements for the contractor to perform 'field engineering,' such as establishing benchmarks and survey control points?
questions.n: Section 01 73 00 includes field engineering and surveying to ensure the project is correctly located and leveled.

questions.q: Under Division 01, if a contractor must drill through a newly installed concrete slab to place a pipe that was missed, which procedure governs this activity?
questions.n: Section 01 73 29 governs the procedural and safety requirements for modifying existing or newly completed work to accommodate other parts of the work.

questions.q: Which administrative document is used by the Architect to provide additional instructions or clarify the contract documents without changing the contract sum or time?
questions.n: An ASI (or Supplemental Instruction) allows the architect to clarify the design intent as long as there is no financial or schedule impact.

questions.q: What is the primary role of the 'Reference Standards' section (01 42 00) in Division 01?
o: To list the contact numbers of all manufacturers
To list all the laws and statutes of the local government
To provide the architect's design references and inspirations
To define abbreviations and explain which version of a standard (like ASTM) applies
questions.n: This section ensures everyone knows which specific version of an industry code is being referenced throughout the specs.

questions.q: If an Architect discovers 'Non-Conforming Work,' what is the primary option available to the Owner according to most General Conditions referenced in Division 01?
o: The Architect can fire the Contractor immediately
The Owner must accept the work as is without any price change
The Owner can accept the work and request a reduction in the contract sum
The Architect must pay to fix the work themselves
questions.n: If the work is usable but doesn't meet the spec, the owner can choose to keep it in exchange for a 'credit' or lower price.

questions.q: Which section of Division 01 would specify the requirements for a 'Construction Progress Schedule' (e.g., using a Gantt Chart or CPM)?
questions.n: Section 01 31 00 or 01 32 00 deals with project management and scheduling logistics.

questions.q: Under 'Temporary Facilities and Controls,' what is the purpose of a 'Weather Protection' requirement?
o: To protect installed work and stored materials from damage by the elements
To determine when the project should be cancelled due to rain
To predict the weather for the contractor's insurance
To keep the architect dry during site visits
questions.n: This ensures that rain, snow, or humidity don't ruin materials like drywall or wood before the building is enclosed.

questions.q: Which of these is a typical 'Life Safety' requirement found in Division 01 during the construction phase?
o: Choosing the color of the exit signs
Hiring a permanent security guard for the finished building
Providing temporary fire extinguishers and egress paths
questions.n: Section 01 50 00 requires the contractor to maintain a safe site, including fire protection and safe exits for workers.

questions.q: When the Architect reviews a 'Sample' submittal, what is their primary objective?
o: To perform a structural stress test on the piece
To keep it as a gift for the owner
To verify the color, texture, and finish against the design intent
To check if the material was bought at the lowest price
questions.n: Physical samples allow the architect to confirm that the aesthetic qualities match what was specified.

questions.q: In Division 01 'Execution' (Section 01 73 00), what does 'Cleaning' refer to?
o: Only the final cleaning before the owner moves in
Both progress cleaning during construction and final cleaning at completion
Washing the contractor's trucks before they leave the site
Cleaning the architect's office during site visits
questions.n: Contractors must keep the site clean daily to prevent hazards and perform a deep clean at the end for the owner.

questions.q: Which milestone defines the point where the project is sufficiently complete for the Owner to occupy it for its intended use, and warranties typically begin?
questions.n: This is a critical legal milestone that shifts responsibility for utilities and insurance and starts the warranty period.

questions.q: If a conflict exists between the Technical Specifications and the Construction Drawings, which document generally takes precedence in standard practice?
questions.n: In the hierarchy of documents, written words in the specifications usually govern over the graphic representations in the drawings.

questions.q: Which term describes a pre-determined amount of money the contractor pays the owner for every day the project is delayed past the completion date?
questions.n: These are not penalties, but a pre-agreed estimate of actual financial loss the owner suffers due to project delays.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of 'Retainage' as specified in Division 01 payment procedures?
o: To provide leverage to ensure the contractor finishes the punch list
To fund the owner's contingency for changes
To pay for the architect's site visits
To cover the cost of project insurance
questions.n: By holding back roughly 5% to 10% of every check, the owner ensures the contractor stays on-site until the very last task is done.

questions.q: In the MasterFormat, where would you find requirements for 'Cutting and Patching' of work already in place?
questions.n: Execution requirements cover the physical handling and modification of the work, including surgical cuts and repairs.

questions.q: Which document authorizes a change in the Work, the Contract Sum, and the Contract Time, and must be signed by the Owner, Contractor, and Architect?
questions.n: A Change Order is the formal legal amendment to the construction contract that all three parties must agree upon.

questions.q: Under Division 01, 'Unit Prices' are most commonly used for which type of work?
o: Items with unknown quantities, like rock excavation or soil removal
questions.n: Since the contractor doesn't know exactly how much rock is underground, they provide a 'price per unit' to be measured later.

questions.q: A 'Construction Change Directive' (CCD) is used when which of the following is true?
o: All parties agree on the price and time change
The Owner needs the work to proceed immediately, but the price is not yet agreed upon
The Contractor refuses to work on the project anymore
The Architect wants to change the building's shape for free
questions.n: A CCD orders the contractor to do the work now, with the price to be settled later through a formula or negotiation.

questions.q: Which section of the Project Manual provides the standard for the 3-Part Section Format (General, Products, Execution)?
questions.n: SectionFormat is the industry standard that dictates every technical spec section must be divided into Part 1, Part 2, and Part 3.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a 'Quantity Allowance' and a 'Cash Allowance'?
o: There is no difference; they are used interchangeably.
Quantity allowances are only for the Architect; Cash is only for the Owner.
Quantity allowances set a fixed amount of material; Cash allowances set a fixed dollar amount.
One is for materials, the other is for labor.
questions.n: Quantity allowances are used when you know the price but not the amount (e.g., 100 extra bricks), while Cash is for unknown price items.
